clue.text: Not favouring writing to the unit on call-up

parts.note: con is the opposite of pro, so it means against or not favouring
script means handwriting or written text
the unit is the number one, written as the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to the draft writes to their regiment when their papers arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: CON (against, as in pros and cons) + SCRIPT + I (one, the unit) + ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Conscription is compulsory enlistment into the armed forces, which is what a call-up is.

clue.text: A weapon made of copper lasts anyway

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: anyway suggests the letters of lasts arranged in any order at all

explanation.surface: A weapon forged from copper will endure whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' is the anagram signal on 'lasts'; 'made of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword once carried by sailors.

clue.text: There's nothing to it!

parts.note: the everyday exclamation that a task is easy is read literally: something whose whole content is nothing

explanation.definitionFit: A nullity is something void or of no substance, a mere nothing.

clue.text: Studies before school to oblige

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart, so studies gives cons
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A pupil must do their homework before going in to class.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to force or compel them, as to oblige them.

clue.text: Popular scene to make an extra page

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a set is the scenery or scene of a play or film

explanation.surface: A magazine adds a page for a fashionable setting.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a separate page or leaf inserted into a book or magazine.

clue.text: Got browned off when glasses were lifted

explanation.surface: Someone got fed up just as everyone raised their glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browned off' is British slang for fed up, but here it means literally browned, as bread under a grill.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread that browned under heat was toasted; when glasses are raised to someone, that person is being toasted at a celebration.

clue.text: Some sporting people who never see the way ahead

definitions.text: Some sporting people who never see the way ahead

parts.words: Some sporting people who never see the way ahead
parts.note: the phrase hints at short-sighted people, but these athletes sit facing backwards as their boat moves forward

explanation.definitionFit: Rowers in a boat face the stern, so they cannot see where they are heading.

clue.text: Regal residence a Roman writer finds a trial

parts.note: a court is the residence of a monarch
Martial was a Roman poet famous for his epigrams

explanation.surface: A classical author discovers a trial taking place at the palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A court-martial is a military judicial hearing for members of the armed forces.

clue.text: A couple of wingers — the one getting loot ran off…

definitions.text: A couple of wingers — the one

indicators.note: off suggests the letters going astray, like the runaway thief, and being jumbled

explanation.surface: Two flyers are introduced, one of them a thief making off with swag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges LOOT RAN. The definition spans this clue and the next: of two birds, this one; 'wingers' are birds, not footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European bunting, a bird once eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: …and the other disputes

parts.note: to spar is to argue or dispute
a row is a noisy dispute

explanation.surface: The second of the pair is quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition continues from the previous clue: the other of the two birds. 'disputes' supplies two synonyms in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small common bird, the second of the two 'wingers'.

clue.text: The man on the gate at the cricket match?

definitions.text: The man on the gate at the cricket match?

parts.words: The man on the gate at the cricket match?
parts.note: the gatekeeper at a ground is suggested, but a cricket wicket is also a kind of gate, and the fielder behind it guards it

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicket is the set of three stumps the batsman defends; a wicket is also a small gate.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder standing behind the stumps to catch the ball keeps the wicket, which is also a word for a little gate.

clue.text: He takes a pragmatic attitude where a catalogue is concerned

parts.note: where ... is concerned means regarding, which is re
a list is a catalogue of items

explanation.surface: A practical person takes a down-to-earth view of a sales catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'where ... is concerned' (meaning regarding) is split around 'a catalogue', so its word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is someone who deals with things as they are, practically rather than idealistically.

clue.text: Bear with male in charge of family representation

parts.note: to tote is to carry or bear

explanation.surface: A bear and a male lead a family portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' is the verb carry, not the animal, though totems often show animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem standing for a clan or kin group, so totemic relates to such an emblem.

clue.text: A Greek character, timid and' over-emotional

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
shy means timid

explanation.surface: A bashful, sentimental figure in a Greek drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushy means sentimental to excess, soppy.

clue.text: Playing a video can offer escape

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Watching a video can be a way to get away from things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges A VIDEO CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoidance is the act of keeping away from or evading something.

clue.text: Went beyond the limit — even port's been ordered

indicators.note: been ordered says the letters have been put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone splashed out too much when even the port has been bought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been ordered' rearranges EVEN PORTS (the 's counts as an S here).
explanation.definitionFit: To have overspent is to have used more money than the budget allows.

clue.text: Alter the siting of the stove at the back

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a large cooking stove

explanation.surface: Move the cooker that stands at the back of the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The stove sits 'at the back', so the word for back stands in front of the stove's word.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange things is to change their positions or order.

clue.text: Refrain that causes a sailor to colour!

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
to stain is to colour

explanation.surface: Song chorus that makes a seaman change colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain' looks like a song's chorus but is the verb hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to hold back from doing something, such as voting or drinking.

clue.text: The leftist getting a blow in is delighted

indicators.note: getting a blow in means the blow is placed inside the word for the leftist

parts.note: a red is a left-winger or communist
a gale is a strong wind, a blow

explanation.surface: The radical is pleased to land a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blow' is wind, not a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To be regaled is to be entertained or treated lavishly, delighted.

clue.text: Point to point say

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
a peak is a pointed summit

explanation.surface: A remark about a point-to-point horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase for hunting horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak is to say words out loud.

clue.text: Boy occupied by press operator

indicators.note: the boy's word is occupied, filled, by the word for press

parts.note: a son is a boy
to urge is to press

explanation.surface: A lad is employed by a printing-press worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operator' is one who operates, a surgeon, not a machine operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon performs operations, so is an operator in the medical sense.

clue.text: London is the — of our times, and the Rome of today." (Emerson)

definitions.text: London is the — of our times, and the Rome of today." (Emerson)

parts.words: London is the — of our times, and the Rome of today." (Emerson)
parts.note: a quotation from Ralph Waldo Emerson with the missing word to be supplied

explanation.definitionFit: Emerson called London the perfect example, the very embodiment, of his age.

clue.text: Visible percipience

explanation.definitionFit: In sight means able to be seen; insight is perceptiveness or deep understanding.

clue.text: A tribute paid in parliament — it heartened a minister

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words parliament it heartened

explanation.surface: A tax levied in the House of Commons was welcome news for a minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across parliamenT IT HEartened.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid as a levy, especially to the church.

clue.text: Do whatever is needed to maintain such a tree

definitions.text: Do whatever is needed to maintain

explanation.surface: Look after a tree properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The service tree is a European tree related to the rowan.
explanation.definitionFit: To service a car or machine is to maintain it; the service tree is a species of Sorbus.

clue.text: Tract of grassland left wild

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassland

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of left running out of control

explanation.surface: A stretch of meadow has been left to grow wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns LEFT into FLET. 'Tract' is a pamphlet, not an area of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, as is a leaflet.

clue.text: Regards metal container as an offensive object

parts.note: to eye something is to regard it
ore is rock that contains metal

explanation.surface: Someone views a tin can as an ugly object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal container' suggests a tin; ore contains metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something ugly to look at.

clue.text: Slip in English and French candle-ends without notice

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these pieces go around the notice

parts.note: in, the English word
and in French, en is the word for in
the first and last letters of candle are C and E
an advert is a notice

explanation.surface: Someone slips up in a bilingual shop sign about candle stubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' works twice over: as the English word and its French equivalent. 'without' has its old sense of outside, so those pieces and the candle's first and last letters surround the notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Inadvertence is a careless lapse, an oversight or slip.
